# Hinge-value sensitivity, geometric bounds, and a sharp endpoint singularity

This note develops the normal stress proved in
candidate 2d0fea5cdbf7c841 (candidate 2d0fea5cdbf7c841).
The fiber family is fixed and consists of positive full-dimensional
polytopes. The cap count `N` is fixed, the continuous normals have length
one, and `v(tau)` is the attained minimum total hinge under full-fiber
coverage and cap masses at most `tau M`. Every symbol below has that
meaning. No body deformation is made.

The new consequences are an exact integrated sensitivity identity, an
explicit but insufficient differential inequality, and divergence of
the sensitivity at the sharp budget for a nonregular simplex product.

## 1. Stress notation and exact total multiplier

At every regular interior feasible budget the preceding theorem gives
nonnegative cap multipliers `r_i`, fiber multipliers `eta_z`, and finite
contact measures on actual saddle pairs `(x,lambda) in K_z x Delta_N`.
Write

`c_i=mu(H_i)`, `Psi_i=int(L_i)_+ dmu`,
`Z_i=int_Hi z dmu`, `X_i=int_Hi x dmu`,
`S_i=int d tau_i`, `Z_i^s=int z d tau_i`, `X_i^s=int x d tau_i`,
`p_zi=int lambda_i d nu_z`, `q_zi=int lambda_i x d nu_z`.

The section measure `tau_i` uses one consistent density between zero
and one on the cap plane, with coarea normalization. Its support has
`L_i=0`. At every multiplied contact, `L_i(z,x)<=0` for all `i` and
`lambda_i L_i(z,x)=0`. The exact equations are

`c_i+r_i S_i=sum_z eta_z p_zi`,                              (1)
`Z_i+r_i Z_i^s=sum_z eta_z z p_zi`,                          (2)
`X_i+r_i X_i^s-sum_z eta_z q_zi=Psi_i u_i`,                  (3)
`M sum_i r_i=-v'(tau)`.                                     (4)

Equation (4) is available because `Psi-v(max_i c_i/M)` has a local
minimum among unbudgeted covers when a budget is active. The explicit
uniform offset coverage repair gives objective multiplier one without
altering this chain-rule coefficient. At a strictly slack minimizing
budget the value is locally flat on its left, its derivative is zero,
and the same equations hold with every `r_i=0`.

## 2. Translation, shear, dilation, and tensor identities

Let `U_z(x,lambda)=sum_i lambda_i u_i`. The contact condition includes
`-U_z in N_Kz(x)`. Summing (1)--(3) gives

`sum_z eta_z=sum_i c_i+sum_i r_i S_i`,                       (5)
`sum_z eta_z z=sum_i Z_i+sum_i r_i Z_i^s`,                    (6)
`sum_z eta_z int x d nu_z
   =sum_i X_i+sum_i r_i X_i^s-sum_i Psi_i u_i`.              (7)

Multiplying (1) by `u_i` and summing yields the continuous translation
balance

`sum_i(c_i+r_i S_i)u_i=sum_z eta_z int U_z d nu_z`.           (8)

The right side is a sum of actual supporting-fiber forces and need not
vanish. Multiplying (2) by `u_i` gives the corresponding affine shear
identity

`sum_i u_i (Z_i+r_i Z_i^s)^T
       =sum_z eta_z int U_z z^T d nu_z`.                    (9)

These are exactly the identities obtained by translating the entire
cap arrangement by an arbitrary continuous affine displacement
`q(z)=Bz+c`: the parameter velocity is
`dot a_i=-B^T u_i`, `dot b_i=u_i dot c`, `dot u_i=0`.
This is a variation of the halfspaces on the fixed source, not a
non-lattice-preserving transformation of the source itself.

There is also the matrix identity

`sum_i [X_i+r_i X_i^s-sum_z eta_z q_zi] u_i^T
       =sum_i Psi_i u_i u_i^T`.                             (10)

Its right side is positive semidefinite and has trace `v(tau)`.
It records all common continuous linear deformations of the cap
arrangement. Indeed, under `x_new=(I+t T)x_old`, restoring each unit
continuous normal gives velocities

`dot u_i=-T^T u_i+(u_i^T T u_i)u_i`,
`dot a_i=(u_i^T T u_i)a_i`,
`dot b_i=(u_i^T T u_i)b_i`.

The section and contact terms arising from the common rescaling vanish
on their cap boundaries. Stationarity for every matrix `T` is (10).
Its scalar trace is the global dilation identity. A dilation about
an affine center `q(z)=Bz+c` instead has

`dot u_i=0`, `dot a_i=a_i+B^T u_i`,
`dot b_i=b_i-u_i dot c`;

its identity is the same trace together with (8)--(9).
The signs here refer to the image of the old halfspaces: the inverse
of `x_new=q+(1+t)(x_old-q)` is
`x_old=(x_new+t q)/(1+t)`. Substitution in the old margin and
multiplication by `1+t` gives exactly the displayed velocities.

At each cap separately the homogeneous Euler equation is
`sigma_i=-Psi_i`, where `sigma_i` is its sphere-normal multiplier.
This is the content of (3). Thus (5)--(10) are exact global consequences
of the per-cap equations, not additional unproved sign conditions.
In particular, (10) does not assert a convex-order comparison between
the source measure and the contact measure.

## 3. Right continuity and integration across exceptional budgets

The value `v` is nonincreasing and is right-continuous at every feasible
budget. To prove the latter, take `tau_k downarrow tau` and attained
minimizers. Their hinges are at most `v(tau)`, so the threshold
compactification from the attainment theorem applies. The limiting
finite cover has cap masses at most `tau M` and hinge
`lim_k v(tau_k)`. Therefore

`v(tau)<=lim_k v(tau_k)<=v(tau)`.

On a compact interval `[a,b]` in the interior feasible domain, `v` is
finite and semialgebraic. It is `C^1` apart from finitely many points,
has finite one-sided limits, and has only downward jumps. On each
regular interval, integrate its nonpositive derivative and pass to
the endpoints by monotone limits. This proves

`v(a)-v(b)
 = M integral_a^b [sum_i r_i(t)] dt
   +sum_(a<t<=b) [v(t-)-v(t)]`.                             (11)

The finite sum can be restricted to discontinuities. The scalar sum
of multipliers in the integral is the unambiguously defined number
`-v'(t)/M`; no measurable selection of the individual stress measures
is required. Derivative singularities at the finitely many exceptional
points are treated by improper integration. Their total integral is
finite on `[a,b]`, because `v` is monotone and finite there.

Thus deleting finitely many budgets from a pointwise first-order
argument does not justify discarding possible value jumps. Formula
(11) is the exact replacement. In particular, it always implies
`M integral_a^b sum_i r_i(t) dt<=v(a)-v(b)`.

## 4. A proved geometric differential inequality

Put `C_0=conv(S)`, with real projection `Q`. Define the compact
symmetric convex body of same-real-base differences

`D_all=conv union_(z in Q) [(C_0)_z-(C_0)_z]`,
`R=max_(v in D_all) |v|>0`.

Compactness follows by taking pairs in the compact set `C_0 x C_0`
with equal base, applying the continuous difference map, and then
taking a convex hull. Positive fibers ensure `R>0`.

For each cap let `W_i=c_i+r_i S_i`. Its source-side measure
`mu|H_i+r_i tau_i` and its contact-side measure from (1)--(3) have
equal mass `W_i`, equal real base first moment, and continuous first
moment difference `Psi_i u_i`. If `W_i>0`, both barycenters lie in
`C_0` and have the same real base. Hence

`(Psi_i/W_i)u_i in D_all`,
`Psi_i<=R W_i`.                                              (12)

If `W_i=0`, then `c_i=0` and `Psi_i=0`, so the same inequality holds.
The sharper directional version replaces `R` by the radial length of
`D_all` in direction `u_i`.

Define a fixed finite section bound

`S_* = sum_(z in P) sup_(|u|=1,t in R)
                  H_(d-1)(K_z intersect {u dot x=t})>0`.

Every effective `S_i<=S_*`, including supporting-facet densities.
Finiteness follows by bounding sections by the projection of a ball
containing the fiber. For `d=1`, each supremum is one.
Summing (12), using `c_i<=tau M`, and then (4), gives

`v(tau)<=R [N tau M-(S_*/M)v'(tau)]`.                        (13)

Equivalently, at every regular budget,

`v'(tau)+A v(tau)<=B tau`,
`A=M/(R S_*)`, `B=N M^2/S_*`.                               (14)

This is a rigorous scalar differential inequality. Downward jumps
only strengthen its integrated form, so for every interior feasible
`a<b`,

`exp(A b)v(b)-exp(A a)v(a)
        <=B integral_a^b t exp(A t) dt`.                    (15)

There is no dimension-only estimate hidden in these coefficients.
Moreover, even their exact values do not make (14) sharp on basic
OC extremizers, as the next calculation demonstrates.

## 5. Exact calibration on an interval product

Take `S={0,1}^n x [0,1]`, `m=2^n`, `M=m`, and `N=2m`.
At every feasible budget `tau>=1/(2m)`,

`v(tau)=m/4`, `v'(tau)=0`.                                  (16)

To prove the lower bound, restrict any full cover to one interval.
Since `|u_i|=1`, every restriction is a ray with slope `+1` or `-1`.
If one ray contains the entire interval its hinge is at least `1/2`.
Otherwise let `a` be the smallest threshold among the increasing
rays and `b` the largest threshold among the decreasing rays. Full
coverage requires `a<=b`. The sum of just those two hinges is at
least `[(1-a)^2+b^2]/2` when both thresholds lie in `[0,1]`, and
this is at least `1/4`, with equality at `a=b=1/2`. If an effective
threshold is outside `[0,1]`, either there is a full ray as above or
it can be clipped to the endpoint, decreasing the hinge and preserving
the coverage relation; the same lower bound follows. Summing over
the disjoint fibers proves `v>=m/4`.

The reverse inequality is attained by the two midpoint rays on each
binary fiber, tilted in the base to be empty on all the other fibers.
There are exactly `2m` caps, each of mass `1/2` and hinge `1/8`.
This also proves the stated feasibility range, because an interval
midpoint on any fiber requires a containing cap of mass at least
`1/2`.

Here `D_all=[-1,1]`, `R=1`, and `S_*=m`. At the exact sharp budget,
the left side of (14) is `m/4` and its right side is `m`. There is a
factor-four slack even on this elementary sharp family. Thus this
particular differential inequality does not recover the OC constant.

## 6. Compactness of normal stresses with bounded budget multipliers

The following strengthening of trace compactification will be useful.
Consider a sequence of covers with bounded hinges. After a subsequence,
all unit continuous normals converge, and every cap's fiber thresholds
have finite limits on a set `I` and tend to positive infinity on its
complement `J`. Choose one affine trace `v` realizing the finite limits,
a bounded right inverse `R_I`, and one kernel trace `h` with `h|I=0`
and all `h|J>0`, as in the attainment proof. If the original finite
trace coordinates are `e_k|I`, replace the whole trace by

`v+R_I(e_k|I-v|I)+T h`,                                     (17)

where the fixed finite `T` is chosen sufficiently large. This preserves
the exact threshold on every fiber in `I` and makes every threshold
in `J` exceed a common radius bound by at least one. Its coefficients
can be chosen bounded, because it ranges in a bounded subset of a
fixed finite-dimensional trace space.

For large `k` the original thresholds on `J` also exceed that bound by
one. Thus original and replacement caps have identical traces on `S`.
Their hinge and cap-mass functions under sufficiently small common
parameter increments are identical as well: the `I` traces agree and
the `J` traces remain strictly empty. The full coverage functions are
also locally identical. An empty trace has margin at most `-1`, whereas
a covering family has pointwise maximum at least zero; sufficiently
small increments keep such a trace irrelevant to the maximum on its
fiber. Consequently the replacement preserves all local cap, hinge,
and coverage generalized-gradient features and the same normal stress.

Suppose now the covers are normal minimizers and `sum_i r_i` is bounded.
Equation (5) and the uniform section bound imply that `sum_z eta_z`
is bounded. The source cap moments, section moments, and contact
features range in compact sets after (17). Taking limits therefore
gives a normal stress for the limiting finite cover. To spell out the
contact issue, for `eta_z>0` the approximating saddle contacts have
`F_z=0`. Every cap with a threshold diverging to infinity is strictly
negative there, so its saddle weight is **exactly zero** for all large
`k`. On all other traces the margins converge uniformly, and (11) of
the normality note survives at the limiting contacts. Consistent
section gradients survive by closedness of the locally Lipschitz
generalized-gradient graph in the bounded replacement parameters.
Equivalently, one can project their section measures and take compact
dominated weak limits. No atom is discarded in either description.

## 7. A necessary singularity at a nonregular simplex-product budget

Let `n>=1,d>=2`, let `K` be a nonregular simplex, put

`S={0,1}^n x K`, `m=2^n`, `N=m(d+1)`,
`tau_0=gamma_d/m`.

The exact sharp-product cover classification and the impossibility
of a normal stress at `tau_0` are proved in
candidate 2a5e48e3badc4c86 (candidate 2a5e48e3badc4c86).
That impossibility also applies to the contact measures used here:
at the sharp budget every active primal contact on a given fiber is
its unique simplex centroid, and the cap weights are supported on
that fiber's own canonical caps. Averaging saddle pairs therefore
does not enlarge the relevant contact geometry.

For the attained hinge value of this product,

`lim_(tau downarrow tau_0, tau regular) [-v'(tau)]=+infinity`.(18)

Indeed, otherwise choose a sequence of regular budgets decreasing to
`tau_0` on which `-v'` is bounded. Select normal minimizers and the
sensitivity-normalized stresses from (4). Their total `r` is bounded.
Their hinges are at most the finite value `v(tau_0)`, and right
continuity from Section 3 shows that their compactified limit is a
sharp-budget minimizing cover. Section 6 passes the bounded stresses
to a normal stress there, contradicting the cited exact obstruction.
This proves (18).

Because `v` is semialgebraic and right-continuous at `tau_0`, this
divergence is integrable: on a sufficiently small interval to its
right there are no further exceptional points, and

`integral_(tau_0)^(tau_0+epsilon) [-v'(t)] dt
          =v(tau_0)-v(tau_0+epsilon)<infinity`.

Thus exact endpoint abnormality is compatible with generic-budget
normality through a divergent, integrable budget sensitivity. It
cannot be removed merely by assuming the cap budget is close to the
sharp one.

## 8. Dependency graph and remaining quantitative gap

The proved chain is

1. Fixed-fiber hinge attainment and semialgebraicity give regular
   budgets with an actual attained value derivative.
2. The explicit coverage repair gives normal stress and the exact
   multiplier sum (4).
3. Same-real-base barycenters give (12); a uniform section bound gives
   the scalar differential inequality (14).
4. Monotonicity, semialgebraicity, and trace compactness give the exact
   integrated identity (11), including all jumps.
5. Sharp-product abnormality plus compact bounded stress gives (18).

The only scalar differential inequality proved here has the explicit
slack in Section 5 and body-dependent coefficients. Improving it to
the required universal OC budget would require a new quantitative
relation among actual small caps, section measures, and cross-fiber
contact measures. Neither a discrete convex-order relation nor a
per-circuit `gamma_d` allocation is supplied or assumed.
